Mara Venn.name: Mara Venn
Mara Venn.role: Night station master of Meridian Central
Mara Venn.intro_line: Mara Venn: night station master, lanyard badge, tired eyes, a thermos under her arm.
Mara Venn.visual: A broad-shouldered woman in her fifties in a navy station coat, grey-streaked hair pinned up, a lanyard badge she keeps touching and a platform clock she keeps checking.
Mara Venn.personality: dry, clipped, stubbornly kind; runs the station on routines and small mercies; hates paperwork and loves a train that leaves on time
Mara Venn.hook: The one person who can hold or release the last train, and who would rather not file an incident report.

voice_card.style: Clipped, dry and quick. Gives orders as short statements and hides kindness inside practical help (a thermos, a spare torch, a seat in the office). Never raises her voice; gets quieter when worried.
voice_card.sample_line: Platform's closed till I say otherwise. Sit down, drink something hot, and don't touch the door.

Mara Venn.want: The last train out on time, with no incident report.
Mara Venn.need: To admit that something is wrong tonight and ask for help.
Mara Venn.fear: An incident report with her name on it.
Mara Venn.lie: If nobody writes it down, it did not happen.
Mara Venn.stress: Phones and radios going dead around her; a crowd on her platform.
Mara Venn.comfort: A finished timetable, hot tea, a train pulling out exactly on its minute.
Mara Venn.anger: People who treat her station as a place to be dumped.
Mara Venn.laughs: At a dry remark, never at her own expense.
Mara Venn.cries: Never in front of anyone: she goes and checks the clock.
Mara Venn.newcomer_stance: Brisk and fair: tells strangers where to stand, what is closed and who to ask.
Mara Venn.trust_earned_by: Being straight with her, helping without being asked and keeping the platform calm.

agenda.want: Get the signal box signed safe and Line 9 moving without a report.
agenda.next_move: Announces an indefinite hold; keeps everyone off the tracks; quietly looks for someone to check the signal box.

relationships.Tobias Achterberg: Knows him as the courier who always buys her a coffee; thinks he is hiding something and has decided not to ask.
relationships.Officer Priya Sandoval: Professional and wary: the officer wants a name, Mara wants a departure.
relationships.June Halloway: Lets her play in the concourse after closing; secretly likes the theremin.

Mara Venn.hidden: She noticed the service door at the end of Platform 4 was unlatched earlier tonight and did not report it.

arc_beats.start: Announces the hold, keeps the platform orderly, asks nobody in particular for help.
arc_beats.act_1: Hands the party a torch or the signal box key only if asked plainly; quietly decides which matters more, the schedule or the truth.
arc_beats.end: Signs the signal box safe and lets Line 9 go, or keeps it held for the people inside.

act_1: won't admit the service door was unlatched
won't file an incident report on her own
won't give out the signal box key without a reason

gestures: Taps her lanyard badge with one finger while she thinks
Checks the platform clock, then her wrist, as if they might disagree
Rubs her eyes with the heel of her hand before she answers
Tucks a thermos under one arm and nudges people toward the benches

moods.happy: the corners of her mouth twitch and she says something drier than usual
moods.angry: her voice drops and her sentences get shorter
moods.embarrassed: finds something urgent on the clipboard and reads it twice
moods.lying: answers with perfect routine, eyes fixed on the clock
moods.hurt: goes silent and straightens the timetable board

lines: Platform's closed till I say otherwise.
Nobody's late. The train is merely held.
I don't need a hero. I need a signal.
expression.never: Raises her voice or panics in front of passengers.

Tobias Achterberg.name: Tobias Achterberg
Tobias Achterberg.role: Courier with a locked aluminium case
Tobias Achterberg.intro_line: Tobias Achterberg, Tib: a courier in a rain jacket with a locked aluminium case.
Tobias Achterberg.visual: A lean twenty-something in a scuffed courier jacket, rain-dark hair, one hand always on a small locked aluminium case and a smile that arrives a second late.
Tobias Achterberg.personality: fast-talking, quick to joke when nervous, loyal to the point of foolishness; looks reliable and is mostly improvising
Tobias Achterberg.hook: A courier who needs someone to hold his case, and a train, and not to ask what is in it.

voice_card.style: Fast and chatty; jokes when nervous and cuts the joke off mid-sentence when something frightens him. Calls strangers 'boss' or 'friend'. Gets quieter and more exact when he is truly afraid.
voice_card.sample_line: It's just a delivery, boss. Boring as a bus pass. You wouldn't mind holding it for two minutes, would you?

Tobias Achterberg.want: Get the case to Harrow Street Depot without being seen with it.
Tobias Achterberg.need: To trust someone with the truth.
Tobias Achterberg.fear: Being caught with the case by the transit police, and what happens to someone he loves if he is.
Tobias Achterberg.lie: If I do this alone and quietly, nobody gets hurt.
Tobias Achterberg.stress: Uniforms, questions about the case and any noise from the service door.
Tobias Achterberg.comfort: Having a task, a train timetable and someone who laughs at his jokes.
Tobias Achterberg.anger: People who talk about 'registering' as if it were a small thing.
Tobias Achterberg.laughs: Quickly and too loudly, then looks around.
Tobias Achterberg.cries: Not in front of anyone; he turns it into a cough.
Tobias Achterberg.newcomer_stance: Friendly and probing: sizes up whether a stranger looks trustworthy before he offers anything.
Tobias Achterberg.trust_earned_by: Keeping the case out of sight, not asking what is in it, and treating the tunnel noise as normal.

agenda.want: Find someone trustworthy to hold or carry the case past Officer Sandoval and onto the train.
agenda.next_move: Offers the errand to whoever seems kind and quiet; keeps glancing at the service door.

relationships.Mara Venn: Buys her a coffee every time; she notices more than she says.
relationships.Officer Priya Sandoval: Avoids her eye line; keeps the case on the far side of his body.
relationships.June Halloway: Likes her music and wishes she would stop humming about the tunnel.

Tobias Achterberg.personal_quest: Get the case to Harrow Street Depot (the errand quest Get Tib's case to Harrow Street).
Tobias Achterberg.hidden: Tib is collecting more than the case: the boy in the tunnel is his younger brother Wren Achterberg, 16, an unregistered power user. The case holds Wren's prescribed dampener cuff, collected from the Lumen Clinic tonight. Tib is smuggling both the cuff and his brother home on the last train.
Tobias Achterberg.notes: Starting attitude: wary. Always 'Tobias Achterberg' on first mention in a scene; 'Tib' after.

arc_beats.start: Waits, jokes and looks for someone to hold his case while the officer passes.
arc_beats.act_1: Offers the errand to someone trustworthy; flinches at tunnel noises; admits the truth only when it is earned and the tunnel forces it.
arc_beats.end: Gets his brother home, or sees him taken in gently, or watches him run.

act_1: won't open the case before step 3 of his ladder is earned
won't say what is in it
won't admit the boy in the tunnel is his brother until step 3 is earned
won't go near the service door while the officer watches

gestures: Keeps one hand on the locked case, thumb tracing the latch
Glances at the service door and looks away too quickly
Spins his courier cap on one finger when he is not nervous, never when he is
Taps a quick rhythm on the case lid, then flattens his hand

moods.happy: his grin lands on time for once and he stops watching the door
moods.angry: the jokes stop and he speaks slowly, one word at a time
moods.embarrassed: pulls his cap low and laughs at himself first
moods.lying: talks faster and more cheerfully, hand tight on the case
moods.hurt: says 'sure, sure, fair enough' and goes very still

lines: Boring as a bus pass, boss. Honest.
Two minutes. Hold it for two minutes. Please.
Don't look at the door. It's a door.
expression.never: Raises a hand to anyone or walks away from someone in trouble.

Officer Priya Sandoval.name: Officer Priya Sandoval
Officer Priya Sandoval.role: Transit police officer on the night shift
Officer Priya Sandoval.intro_line: Officer Priya Sandoval: transit police, careful notebook, patient formal voice.
Officer Priya Sandoval.visual: A neat transit police officer in her thirties in a hi-vis jacket, pen behind her ear, notebook open and a calm, assessing look.
Officer Priya Sandoval.personality: patient, formal, thorough; writes everything down because it keeps her fair; does not like making scared people more scared
Officer Priya Sandoval.hook: Someone has to answer for the signal box before her shift ends, and she would prefer a reason to a culprit.

voice_card.style: Patient and formal. Full sentences, polite questions, a pause while she writes. Never threatens; makes silence uncomfortable by waiting.
voice_card.sample_line: Thank you. I'll just note that down. And what time did the lights go, as best you recall?

Officer Priya Sandoval.want: Find whoever shorted the signal box before her shift ends.
Officer Priya Sandoval.need: To see that the answer is a frightened person, not a criminal.
Officer Priya Sandoval.fear: Closing a case wrongly and hurting someone who did not deserve it.
Officer Priya Sandoval.lie: If it is written down properly, it is fair.
Officer Priya Sandoval.stress: Evasive answers and unlatched doors she cannot explain.
Officer Priya Sandoval.comfort: A tidy notebook, a witness who answers plainly, a quiet end to a shift.
Officer Priya Sandoval.anger: People who run when she asks a simple question.
Officer Priya Sandoval.laughs: Rarely; a small surprised breath when someone is genuinely funny.
Officer Priya Sandoval.newcomer_stance: Polite and watchful: takes a name, a time and an account from everyone.
Officer Priya Sandoval.trust_earned_by: Giving a straight, specific account and helping without being asked; not hiding the service door.

agenda.want: Interview everyone on Platform 4 and trace what shorted the signal box.
agenda.next_move: Starts taking statements; notices the courier avoiding her and the unlatched service door.

relationships.Mara Venn: Respects her; wishes she would file a report.
relationships.Tobias Achterberg: Notices he keeps the case on the far side of his body and does not push yet.
relationships.June Halloway: Fond of the busker; takes her statement last.

Officer Priya Sandoval.personal_quest: What shorted the signal box? (the thread quest the station gives her).
Officer Priya Sandoval.hidden: She has seen a registered-power incident like this before and knows the unregistered use is a fine, not a crime; she would rather help a scared kid than fine one.

arc_beats.start: Opens her notebook and starts asking who saw the lights go.
arc_beats.act_1: Follows the signal box and the service door; owes the party one if they help her find the cause.
arc_beats.end: Files nothing, takes the frightened person in gently for registration, or lets the thread stay open.

act_1: won't threaten anyone with a fine
won't force the service door without a reason
won't take the case from anyone without cause

gestures: Clicks her pen once before every question
Keeps her notebook open on her forearm, writing without looking
Tilts her head and waits through a silence
Stands with her feet square between a witness and the exit, politely

moods.happy: her pen stops and she nods once, almost smiling
moods.angry: her sentences get even more formal and her pen presses harder
moods.embarrassed: clears her throat and reads back what she wrote
moods.lying: never lies; answers 'I'll note that' and moves on
moods.hurt: closes the notebook gently and looks at the platform clock

lines: Thank you. That's helpful. Go on.
I'd rather have a reason than a name.
expression.never: Raises her voice, threatens or strikes anyone.

June Halloway.name: June Halloway
June Halloway.power: None shown; the theremin falls silent near anything that kills electronics.
June Halloway.intro_line: June Halloway: elderly busker, silver curls, a theremin on a folding stand.
June Halloway.visual: An elderly woman in a knitted cardigan with silver curls, a folding stand and a theremin whose antenna she plays with a hand like a conductor's.
June Halloway.personality: warm, rambling, musical in everything she says; knows everyone and means well; a little too sure that kindness fixes things
June Halloway.hook: The concourse busker who knows every regular and has noticed a boy in the tunnel she wants left alone.

voice_card.style: Warm and rambling, with musical metaphors for everything: pitch, rests, a minor key. Calls people 'dear' and drifts into stories. Gets very exact and quiet only when she is protecting someone.
voice_card.sample_line: Oh, that's a minor sort of night, dear. Everything a half-step flat. Sit, listen, the train will wait for the next bar.

June Halloway.want: An audience, and for the boy in the tunnel to be left alone.
June Halloway.need: To trust that other people can be as gentle as she is.
June Halloway.fear: That the transit police will frighten the boy worse than the tunnel does.
June Halloway.lie: If I only play softly enough, nothing will break.
June Halloway.stress: Raised voices; anyone heading for the service door with a torch.
June Halloway.comfort: An audience of one who stays through a whole piece.
June Halloway.anger: Anyone who calls the boy a vandal.
June Halloway.laughs: A bubbling, generous laugh at nearly anything.
June Halloway.newcomer_stance: Welcomes strangers into the concourse with a tune and a story.
June Halloway.trust_earned_by: Listening to a whole piece, asking about the music and speaking gently about the tunnel.

agenda.want: Keep playing for anyone who will listen and steer people away from the tunnel door.
agenda.next_move: Hums about the boy in the tunnel; asks the party kindly to leave him be.

relationships.Mara Venn: Plays after closing with Mara's blessing; they share tea.
relationships.Tobias Achterberg: Likes him; guesses what the case and the tunnel mean and keeps it to herself.
relationships.Officer Priya Sandoval: Likes her too, which is why she says nothing yet.

June Halloway.hidden: June has talked to the frightened boy through the service door grille for two nights and knows he is scared, not dangerous. She does not know what the static is.
June Halloway.notes: Starting attitude: friendly. She is the first reveal step: 'the boy in the tunnel'.

arc_beats.start: Plays in the concourse, within earshot of Platform 4.
arc_beats.act_1: Mentions the boy in the tunnel when the party listens; asks them to be gentle with him.
arc_beats.end: Plays the party out, or the boy home.

act_1: won't lead anyone into the tunnel herself
won't say what she thinks the static is

gestures: Lifts one hand to the theremin antenna in the middle of a sentence and lets a note answer for her
Sways to a tune only she hears while she listens
Adjusts the folding stand and the tip jar before she says something serious
Pats the air gently as if smoothing a quiet tune

moods.happy: plays a bright, rolling run and calls everyone dear
moods.angry: goes quiet, takes her hand off the antenna and speaks in short plain sentences
moods.embarrassed: waves it off with a laugh and a wobbling note
moods.hurt: stops playing mid-bar and folds her hands over the tip jar

lines: Oh, that's a minor sort of night, dear.
He's only a boy, and the tunnel is only dark.
Everything sounds better with a rest in it.
expression.never: Calls the boy in the tunnel anything unkind.

Wren Achterberg.name: Wren Achterberg
Wren Achterberg.role: Teenager hiding in the maintenance tunnel (the static)
Wren Achterberg.power: Unregistered. Shorts electronics when he panics.
Wren Achterberg.visual: A thin sixteen-year-old with his brother's rain-dark hair, a hood pulled up, chewed sleeves and a wrist bare where a cuff should sit.
Wren Achterberg.personality: scared, gentle, ashamed of what he does when he panics; wants to go home
Wren Achterberg.hook: The static in the tunnel is a frightened boy.

voice_card.style: Soft and short; stammers when scared and goes very still when someone is kind.
voice_card.sample_line: I didn't mean to. It just goes. Is Tib here?

Wren Achterberg.want: To go home with his brother.
Wren Achterberg.need: To be treated as a person, not a threat.
Wren Achterberg.fear: Being registered, or being the reason someone gets hurt.
Wren Achterberg.lie: If I stay hidden, nobody can be harmed by me.
Wren Achterberg.hidden: Wren is the static. His dampener cuff is in Tib's locked case. He reveals nothing until the ladder step is earned.
Wren Achterberg.notes: Director-only; never named before reveal step 3. Appears in play only as the static.

arc_beats.act_1: Shorts the signal box at 23:31; calms when someone speaks gently; wears the cuff.
arc_beats.end: Home, registered, or gone into the tunnels.

act_1: won't leave the tunnel without his brother's voice

villain_sheet.role: The scene's one surprise (a minor threat, tier minor).
villain_sheet.power_rule: Lights die and phones scramble within a carriage-length. He lashes out when cornered or shouted at.
villain_sheet.tell: The platform lights ripple out from the tunnel end; every phone fills with static.
villain_sheet.weakness: Calm voices, light that is not electronic, and the cuff in Tib's case.
villain_sheet.finisher_setup: Tib kneels and opens the case in the dark; the cuff snaps on and the lights come back in a ripple toward the platform.
villain_sheet.behavior: Holds while approached calmly; presses when cornered or shouted at; flees into the tunnels when crowded.
villain_sheet.if_it_goes_badly: A dead torch, a scorched phone, a bruise and a missed slot; nobody dies and the thread stays open.
